input.quote: 13.1 IBM assumes and will assume ownership and MSL assigns and will assign all intellectual and industrial property rights for hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered under this Agreement
input.rationale: No licence runs from MSL (Vendor) to IBM (Customer) that could be revocable or exclude our affiliates/contractors. Instead, Section 13.1 vests outright ownership in IBM by assignment of all IP in the hardware, software, design and documentation of Products, and 13.2 confirms IBM receives no MSL confidential information; Section 13.0's only reservation to MSL (p0198) is a narrow right to use assigned inventions in performing its own obligations, plus a bar on MSL injecting proprietary processes. Ownership exceeds every preferred element: it is inherently perpetual, irrevocable, not terminable at MSL's discretion, and freely transferable to IBM's successors, and it lets IBM extend rights to contractors (reinforced by 5.2(a)(ii), under which MSL must transfer responsibilities and Products "to IBM or to another party that IBM designates"). Affiliate coverage is already built in: clause 1.9 defines "IBM" as International Business Machines Corporation "and its Subsidiaries", so adding affiliate wording would be duplicative. The licences in 13.3(a), the Loan Agreement (Sections 5 and 6) and Attachment 6 run from IBM to MSL and are restrictions on the Vendor that benefit us, so they are not flagged. The mutual sentence in 24.1(a) that "MSL conveys to IBM no software title or license under the intellectual property rights of MSL or of any third party" is a reciprocal no-implied-licence statement in the I/T system-access context, not a grant clause, and does not cut into IBM's ownership of Product IP. The only wording short of the preferred template is the absence of an express "contractors acting on IBM's behalf" phrase, which is a drafting nicety here rather than a material gap given IBM's ownership; noted, not redlined.
